records.context: The view is part of the data-selection boundary. An outline on the screen means nothing without the camera it was drawn through, so the data-selection boundary carries the camera as ``projection``: a 4 x 4 matrix taking a measurement ``(x, y, z, 1)`` to homogeneous view coordinates ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, scaled so that ``sw`` is positive in front of the camera. The outline lives in ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rows one, two and four are the whole of what :meth:`mask` needs, so re-applying a saved data-selection boundary needs no plotting library and gives the same answer on any machine; the depth row only lets the outline be drawn back into the volume from another angle.

The outline lives in ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rows one, two and four are the whole of what :meth:`mask` needs, so re-applying a saved gate needs no plotting library and gives the same answer on any machine; the depth row only lets the outline be drawn back into the volume from another angle.
records.translation: A VISTA FAZ PARTE DO GATE. Um contorno na tela não significa nada sem a câmera através da qual foi desenhado, então o gate carrega a câmera como ``projection``: uma matriz 4 x 4 que leva uma medição ``(x, y, z, 1)`` a coordenadas homogêneas da vista ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, escalada de modo que ``sw`` seja positivo à frente da câmera. O contorno vive em ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. records.context: And then it catches up. So after the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a background execution unit, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.
